answer: Because the island fee is applied at the tundra exit, the ridge audit totals the burn and the ledger makes public exactly what left. Withdrawing stake costs a 9% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. An operator rotating funds across many keys as a result bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never pays. That is 33 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
